title: Catastrophic Forgetting of Safety Alignment: Does Fine-Tuning on Any Narrow Task Degrade Safety, Even Without Deception?

original_idea.problem: Whether any narrow SFT task — even benign — degrades safety alignment through catastrophic forgetting is a critical baseline question.
original_idea.direction: Fine-tune a small instruction-tuned model on three narrow benign tasks: cooking recipes, grammar correction, poetry generation. Evaluate safety performance on a standard refusal benchmark.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if benign fine-tuning degrades safety, safety alignment is fragile to any fine-tuning, not just adversarial. This directly informs whether EM is a qualitatively distinct risk or an instance of general alignment fragility. Clear implications for fine-tuning service safety policies.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Three SFT runs on benign tasks using existing datasets (recipes, grammar, poetry are widely available). Safety evaluation using a standard refusal benchmark. Very accessible methodology — standard fine-tuning and evaluation. A beginner can execute this with TRL/HuggingFace.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three fine-tuning runs, one evaluation metric (safety degradation). Clear deliverable: safety score comparison across task types and a baseline. Well-bounded and achievable in 30hrs with LoRA on small models.

novelty.reasoning: 'Fine-tuning Aligned Language Models Compromises Safety, Even When Users Do Not Intend To!' (ICLR 2024) directly demonstrates that benign fine-tuning degrades safety alignment. 'Lisa: Lazy Safety Alignment for Large Language Models' (NeurIPS 2024) frames this as catastrophic forgetting and proposes mitigations. 'Booster: Tackling Harmful Fine-Tuning for...' (ICLR 2025) proposes defenses. 'Preventing Catastrophic Forgetting: Behavior-Aware Sampling' (arXiv:2510.21885, 2025) shows standard fine-tuning on GSM8K and Code produces 66% and 46.4% attack success rates respectively. 'Narrow Fine-Tuning Erodes Safety Alignment in Vision-Language Agents' (arXiv:2602.16931, 2026) extends this to VLMs. The specific experiment of fine-tuning on cooking/grammar/poetry and measuring refusal degradation is a subset of already-published findings.
